title: Finite algebras over Hausdorff extremally disconnected affine spectra
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings and R -> S an algebra map. Assume S is finite as an R-module and finitely presented as an R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Suppose Spec R [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is Hausdorff and extremally disconnected, and every residue field kappa(p), for p in Spec R, is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]. Then Spec S is extremally disconnected. No flatness, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0985, Lemma 61.11.5, finite case; expand the decomposition using the finite affine section-cover theorem (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0985).

proof.text: Put X=Spec R and Y=Spec S. The Hausdorff spectrum X has only maximal primes. Apply the finite affine section-cover theorem to Y -> X to obtain a finite locally free surjection a:X_prime -> X, a finite locally free W over X_prime, a closed embedding j:Y_prime -> W where Y_prime=Y times_X X_prime, and finitely many closed sections of W covering its points. Every prime of these finite affine schemes is maximal by integrality, so their spaces are compact Hausdorff and zero-dimensional.

The closed embedding j is finitely presented: Y_prime -> X is finitely presented and W -> X is of finite type, so apply Mathlib RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_comp_finiteType on these affine schemes. Chevalley (Scheme.Hom.isConstructible_image) makes its image constructible, hence clopen in the zero-dimensional affine W. Each section has a clopen incidence locus with this image. The equalizer locus of two sections is also clopen, by the finitely presented closed diagonal of the finite locally free map W -> X_prime and the same constructible-image argument. Partition X_prime into the finitely many clopen Boolean atoms cut out by these incidence and equality loci. On each atom select one representative of every section-equivalence class lying in Y_prime. Their images are disjoint and cover Y_prime on that atom.

The compact Hausdorff surjection a has a continuous section sigma by projectivity of the extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space X. Pull the finite clopen partition of X_prime back along sigma. Each resulting clopen piece C of X is again extremally disconnected.

For x in X, x_prime=sigma(x), and y in Y above x, the points of Y_prime over (y,x_prime) are the primes of kappa(y) tensor_(kappa(x)) kappa(x_prime), by Scheme.Pullback.carrierEquiv. The extension kappa(y)/kappa(x) is algebraic because Y -> X is finite. Since kappa(x) is separably closed, Mathlib Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isPurelyInseparable_of_isSepClosed makes it purely inseparable. Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_tensorProductMap_of_isPurelyInseparable and the tensor left-unit equivalence identify the spectrum of the tensor product homeomorphically with Spec kappa(x_prime), a singleton. This calculation is already Lean-proved in the private subsingleton_primeSpectrum_tensor_of_isSepClosed helper in the new module. The selected sections restricted along sigma therefore define a continuous bijection from finitely many copies of each C onto the part of Y above C. Compactness and Hausdorffness make it a homeomorphism. The private tripletTensor_subsingleton and pullbackPoint_ext helpers additionally implement the field-tensor comparison and point uniqueness via Scheme.Pullback.carrierEquiv, under the indicated residue-integrality hypothesis.

Finite disjoint unions of extremally disconnected spaces are extremally disconnected (the sigma-type instance). The homeomorphisms of the preceding step therefore make Y extremally disconnected. Empty spectra and empty Boolean atoms cause no exception. No flatness or reducedness of S was used.
